title: Developing with muructl run
description: Guided JupyterLab workshops on developing a Flask, Django or FastAPI project under muructl run: where its settings live, what each framework needs, the hooks around the fork, reload and HTTPS fitted to a real project, what happens when a request hangs, and a request stopped at a breakpoint.

workshops.name: settings-in-the-project
workshops.title: Keep the run settings with the project
workshops.description: Move a long muructl run command line into the project's [tool.muru] table, put how a checkout is served into [tool.muru.run] and one machine's own port into muru.local.toml, see what a flag or a misspelt key does, and what --print-config makes of it all for the daemon, compared with where gunicorn, uvicorn, Granian and mod_wsgi keep their settings.

workshops.name: serving-a-flask-project
workshops.title: A Flask project under muructl run
workshops.description: Serve a Flask project built by an application factory under muructl run, see why the factory has to be named as one, give each worker a database pool of its own and see what sharing one from the host means, turn on the project's own logging, let Muru answer for a failing view, and hand the static files from Flask to the edge, compared with what flask run, gunicorn and mod_wsgi do with a factory.

workshops.name: serving-a-django-project
workshops.title: A Django project under muructl run
workshops.description: Serve a Django project from its wsgi.py under muructl run, reloading on each change, find out why the admin has no styles outside runserver and serve its static files in development, choose between Django's debug page and Muru's error page for a failing view, then serve the same project from asgi.py and see where sync and async views run, compared with runserver, gunicorn, uvicorn and mod_wsgi.

workshops.name: fastapi-on-the-event-loop
workshops.title: FastAPI and Starlette on the event loop
workshops.description: Serve a FastAPI application under muructl run and find out what runs where on a worker's event loop, from the lifespan that runs once in each worker to async def, plain def and asyncio.to_thread path operations under load, then block the loop and watch the loop stall timeout replace the worker, compared with uvicorn and gunicorn.

workshops.name: every-hook-in-order
workshops.title: Hooks from load to exit
workshops.description: Run a hooks module with all seven of Muru's lifecycle hooks and read from the terminal where and when each one runs, through startup, a reload that replaces the workers, a signal to reopen logs, workers that import the application themselves, and an ASGI application's lifespan, compared with gunicorn's server hooks.

workshops.name: reload-and-https-your-way
workshops.title: Reload and HTTPS beyond the defaults
workshops.description: Make a development run's reload watch a project's templates and data files and ignore the file it writes, watch a request in flight finish on the old release during a reload, put another name on the development certificate, redirect HTTP to HTTPS, serve a certificate from a CA of your own, then move every flag into the project's run table, compared with gunicorn's and uvicorn's options.

workshops.name: when-a-request-hangs
workshops.title: When a request hangs
workshops.description: Find out what Muru does with a request that never finishes, from the soft timeout that interrupts Python code and says where it was, to the hard timeout that replaces a worker whose code swallows it and the GIL stall timeout that replaces one stuck in C code holding the GIL, and keep the access log to what needs attention, compared with gunicorn, uvicorn and mod_wsgi.

workshops.name: stopping-at-a-breakpoint
workshops.title: Stop a request at a breakpoint
workshops.description: Put breakpoint() in a request served by muructl run, see the worker wait for a debugger while the timeouts stand aside, attach pdb to it from another terminal, read and change what the request is about to do, let it go on, watch a breakpoint nobody attaches to expire, and open a session in a worker with no breakpoint waiting, compared with what breakpoint() does under flask run, runserver, gunicorn and mod_wsgi.
